Download the ‘FL_baseline_metadata_and_annual_results.parquet’ file and save this file into an appropriate folder. 4. Using an integrated development environment (IDE), such as Jupyter Notebook or Visual Studio Code (VSCode), create/initialize a Python programming environment in the same folder where the ‘FL_baseline_metadata_and_annual_results.parquet’ file was saved in Step 2. 5. Import the Pandas library using the code below. Note: Based on the IDE you use, you may first need it to locally install the Pandas library before your import it into the Python code14. import pandas as pd 6. Convert the ‘FL_baseline_metadata_and_annual_results.parquet’ file into a pandas dataframe (florida_df) using the code below. Note: All subsequent data processing uses the features in the Pandas library to process the data. florida_df = pd.read_parquet('FL_baseline_metadta_and_annual_results.parquet') 7. Create a new dataframe (pbc_bldgs) by filtering out all the buildings in Palm Beach County from the ‘florida_df’ dataframe using the code below. pbc_bldgs = florida_df[(florida_df['in.county_name']=='Palm Beach County')] This dataframe (pbc_bldgs) now contains a representative sample of all residential buildings in PBC. Using the tools built into the Pandas library it is possible to very quickly do many different types of data analysis on this dataframe. Appendix B Additional client provided data There were several additional relevant data points found in the local building stock data that are not available in the ResStock data. From Florida International University’s Palm Beach County Affordable Housing Needs Assessment, an analysis of cost burdened households was presented. Cost burdened and severely cost burdened households are defined as households that spend more than 30% and 50%, respectively, of their annual income on housing costs. Table B-1 and Table B-2 outline the cost burdened data presented in that assessment. Table B-1: Palm Beach County: Monthly owner costs as percentage of household income, 2018 Table B-2: Palm Beach County gross rent as a percentage of renter household income, 2010–2018 Additionally, the Palm Beach County Housing Equity Study developed by FIU gave some insights into the racial disparities in PBC, which are not captured in the ResStock data. Figure B-1 and Figure B-2 shows the geographic distribution of Black, non-Hispanic and Hispanic, of any race household across PBC, respectively. Figure B-3 shows the relative percentage of occupancy in different building types by race. 21 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications.
